1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 c5 4.exd5 Qxd5 5.N.strategy: Attacks the queen with a developing move. The pawn on e6 guards it, but a queen for a bishop is no trade, so Black must move it. White gains a tempo, keeps the lead in development and has the d4 pawn to recover.

Keeps the queen in the centre, out of the bishop's reach and still guarding d4. White's knight can jump to e4 with a tempo on it, so Black has to develop a knight to f6 to stop that; after that he is solid, with the extra central pawn.

Retreats the queen all the way home. It still guards d4, but Black has moved the queen twice and White uses the time to finish development before winning the pawn back. Safe but passive: Black keeps the extra central pawn and gives up the initiative.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 c5 4.exd5 Qxd5 5.N.name: French Defence: Tarrasch Variation, Eliskases Variation
